parsed.explanation: Parent national regime applies directly to the island with no documented local mitigation. Main traveller exposure is tier-1 custody placement by identity-document marker, placing trans women in all-male facilities where threatened, corroborated by the 2021 watchdog finding of persistent serious violations across all detention places. No trans-specific criminalisation, border targeting, or facility ban is documented, and national anti-discrimination and transphobia-aggravator law provide formal recourse, but island enforcement of those protections is not documented, local legal help is thin, and lived experience diverges from written law on a conservative island. Youth-care status is unresolved. This sits in Elevated Risk: severe if detained, otherwise no documented visitor-facing criminal exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Document marker governs later custody placement; no documented border refusal or marker mismatch at entry.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No visitor document-acceptance rule stated.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport marker, if checked at entry, becomes operative if any detention or facility placement follows.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans detainees placed by ID-document gender in all-male facilities where threatened; watchdog found persistent serious fundamental-rights violations across all places of deprivation of liberty.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented working remedy for placement or violations; watchdog reporting corroborates unremedied exposure.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Applies directly to island jails as state establishments, not only mainland facilities inspected.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter, or public-facility rule for visitors is stated.

care_services.exposure: Healthcare found to suffer lack of self-determination, long waits and inequitable access by location; visitor HRT continuity not documented.
care_services.protection: Treatment funded under national long-term-condition scheme for residents; no visitor rule documented.
care_services.interaction: Location inequity may affect island access, but visitor-specific consequence is undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence, cross-dressing or presentation law documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National law bans gender-identity discrimination in penal and labour codes; transphobia is aggravating factor since 2017.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal protections are national but island enforcement is not documented, so they do not offset custody exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Legislation to ban medical transition under 18 passed senate May 2024, opposed by government, unresolved after 23 July 2024.
minors_guardians.protection: Late-2024 paediatric guidelines recommend puberty blockers from Tanner stage 2; no operative visitor/minor ban documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor travelling with guardian faces uncertain care-acquisition status; adult guardian risks are as for adults.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No island-specific trans violence data documented; 2020 national combined homophobic/transphobic figure cannot establish island rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Transphobia aggravator and hate-crime provisions are formal recourse; police response on island not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Conservative social climate may increase friction, but documented evidence is social-context only, not island incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No local LGBT-friendly lawyer referenced for island towns; mainland lawyer listed as available. Watchdog persistence since referrals from 2010 through 2021 shows no documented correction.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Mainland-based high-court lawyer available; national remedies exist in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remote/remedy gap compounds custody exposure if detention occurs.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower-risk than 0.25-C: that anchor adds cross-dressing criminalisation and raids plus birth-sex prison placement. Here no presentation crime or targeting is documented and formal protections exist, so score is materially above 0.25 despite similar custody placement.

Similar to but slightly below 0.55-C: both centre on marker-based placement with uneven remedies. Here placement is custodial, with watchdog-documented threats and serious violations, which is more severe than ward denial, pulling below 0.55.

Lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has brief border hold followed by working apology/compensation and reliable court release. Here no working remedy for the documented custody violations is shown, and local legal access is thin, so protections do not operate equivalently.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national protections coexist with a directly operative, document-based custody system that watchdog evidence shows persistently harms trans detainees. A traveller not detained faces no documented criminalisation or facility ban and has formal national recourse, but a traveller who is detained for any reason faces severe, state-imposed exposure with no documented island remedy. That conditional tier-1 exposure, plus thin local legal support and social divergence from written law, places the case in Elevated Risk, below jurisdictions with demonstrated working remedies and above those with active targeting or presentation crimes.
